newsitem.title: UK: C&W Communications flexes financial muscles.
newsitem.headline: C&W Communications flexes financial muscles.

text.p: Britain's Cable and Wireless Communications, the merger between four cable companies, said on Monday it had secured substantial financial headroom over and above its immediate expenditure plans.

Announcing its formal formation and partial flotation plans in a hefty 800-page document, the company said it had secured a 2.9 billion interim credit facility at very attractive rates to refinance its existing debt and to fund its capital expenditure programme.

Cable and Wireless Communications, which has been formed by merging Cable and Wireless Plc's Mercury unit with three UK cable television subsidiaries of NYNEX Corp and Bell Canada, remained tight-lipped about most synergy savings ahead of its float.

But finance director Nicholas Mearing-Smith told a news conference that interest rate agreements on the credit facility, at two basis points below previous debt repayment agreements, would save the group around 20 million pounds per year.

The new company, which will float a 14.7 percent stake on the London and New York stock exchanges in the next few weeks, would also save well over 100 million stg over two years previously spent on taxes by offsetting the cable companies' losses against Mercury's profits.

The new cable giant also said synergy savings would be substantial and included rationalisating its 12,500 workforce and capital expenditure plans, eliminating duplications and reducing interconnect payments to British Telecommunications Plc.
"We have an enormous potential to increase efficiencies," non-executive chairman Richard Brown said.

The merged group will have shareholder equity of 2.3 billion stg, net debt of 1.3 billion stg and interest cover of 2.6 times. Proforma pre-tax profits jumped from 46 million stg in 1996 to 93 million in the nine months of 1997.

Proforma earnings per share doubled to 6 pence in the last nine months compared to the 12 months of 1996. The company does not plan to pay a dividend and proposes instead to use its cash flow for capital investment.

These will total 2.07 billion stg over the next two years, including 110 million stg to build out its digital infrastructure and an estimated 180 million stg to invest in set-top boxes, the group said.
Fixed assets are worth around 4.5 billion stg, chief executive Graham Wallace said.
"The result (of the merger) will be a whole that is much greater than the sum of the parts," finance director Mearing-Smith said.

The group plans to aggressively grow its telephony and entertainment market share and put customer service first. Currently, Cable and Wireless Communications will have 10 percent of the 21 billion stg UK telecoms market and a three percent share of the 2.6 billion stg multichannel TV and entertainment market.
It wants to double the number of homes passed by its network to six million by 2001.
